Point release on top of [v2.0](../../releases/tag/v2.0). One behavioural change,
plus the measured result of running it.

Same warnings as v2.0 apply: personal fork, developed and tested on one machine
with one powder, dispensing gunpowder charges - verify weights independently.

| File | Board | |
|---|---|---|
| `opentrickler-v2.1-pico2_w.uf2` | Raspberry Pi Pico **2** W (RP2350) | developed and tested on this |
| `opentrickler-v2.1-pico_w.uf2` | Raspberry Pi Pico W (RP2040) | **builds, but untested** |

**No EEPROM change from v2.0** - settings and profiles carry over, and there is
no need to re-run Learn Powder.

## Live tuning can now raise the landing speed

In v2.0 the per-throw tuner had no path to increase
`fine_min_flow_speed_rps`. The only line touching it was a 0.85x reduction when
a throw went over, so it was a one-way ratchet. Fine-phase time runs at roughly

    3 x fine_lag x (ln(fine max / fine min) + 1)

which makes the landing speed the dominant term in how long a throw takes. Every
overthrow therefore cost time permanently, and no run of clean throws could earn
it back.

The tuner now keeps a 12-throw window of errors - every throw, so misses count -
and on each clean streak compares the margin it is actually observing
(`bracket / sd`) against the **Landing Sigma** you asked for, scaling the landing
speed by that ratio. Movement is capped at 15% per adjustment and still bounded
to 50-140% of the fitted value.

That ratio is a direct correction rather than a guess: landing error scales
linearly with landing speed, confirmed on hardware when halving the speed halved
the measured spread exactly. The loop is self-correcting in both directions, since
landing too fast widens the spread, which lowers the observed margin, which pulls
the speed back down.

It also recovers headroom the fit leaves on the table. Learn sizes the landing
speed from the lag spread measured during its calibration ladder, at speeds the
tube never actually lands at, so it reads conservative - asking for 2 sigma of
margin produced 2.6 in practice.

## Measured over 84 consecutive throws

Two sessions, +/-0.06 gr bracket, one powder, one machine. **84 throws, 84
inside the bracket, no over and no under.**

| | 36-throw run (26.5 gr) | 48-throw run (30 and 42.5 gr) |
|---|---|---|
| Inside bracket | 36 / 36 | **48 / 48** |
| Mean error | -0.0138 gr | -0.0296 gr |
| Spread (sd) | 0.0325 gr | 0.0278 gr |
| Observed margin | 1.85 sigma | 2.16 sigma |
| Throw time | 10.3 s | 9.3 s average |

The loop converges and then holds. Over the 48-throw run:

| | throw time | fine phase |
|---|---|---|
| first 10 | 10.00 s | 8.60 s |
| middle | 8.83 s | 7.42 s |
| last 10 | **8.85 s** | 7.42 s |

It finds an operating point in roughly 10-15 throws, settles there, and stops
moving - which is the behaviour this change was for. The landing speed is not
driven until something breaks; it stops when the spread it observes matches the
margin asked for.

## Known: a systematic offset worth about half a bracket

Across the 48-throw run the mean error is **-0.0296 gr** against a
`fine_stop_threshold` of 0.030 gr, and errors run from -0.060 to +0.030 - all
the slack sits on the under side, with six throws landing exactly on the bracket
edge. Nothing failed, and undershoot is the safe direction, but centring that
distribution would hand back roughly 0.03 gr of margin that could be spent on a
faster landing instead. Not addressed in this release.
